nodes.name: IF Cleaning
nodes.procedure: The IF was cut into pieces (10 mm × 20 mm × 1 mm) and cleaned by sequential ultrasonication in a 1 M HCl solution, ethanol, and ultrapure water for 15 min.

nodes.name: NiFe-LDH Corrosion Growth
nodes.procedure: The cleaned IF was placed in 30 mL of a 0.1 M Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O aqueous solution and left undisturbed at room temperature for 24 h. After corrosion, the obtained NiFe-LDH/IF was rinsed with ultrapure water and dried in a vacuum dryer at room temperature.

nodes.name: Ni Magnetron Sputtering
nodes.procedure: A pure Ni thin film was deposited onto NiFe-LDH/IF by direct current (DC) magnetron sputtering. During deposition, the DC power applied to the target was maintained at 300 W. Ni/NiFe-LDH/IF was synthesized by directly depositing pure Ni onto the NiFe-LDH/IF system at a total pressure of 0.5 Pa under Ar flow (20 sccm) for 30 min.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LDH/IF shows crimped nanosheets forming urchin-like structure with multiple interspaces; Ni/NiFe-LDH/IF maintains flake-like morphology after Ni deposition with average nanosheet thickness ~310 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figures 1b and S2, crimped NiFe-LDH nanosheets grew uniformly on the IF, forming an urchin-like structure with multiple interspaces. According to the SEM images (Figures 1c and S3), the flake-like morphology of Ni/NiFe-LDH/IF was well maintained after the deposition of the metallic Ni layer, while the average nanosheet thickness increased to approximately 310 nm (Figure S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni/NiFe-LDH shows coarse Ni metal layer homogeneously distributed across NiFe-LDH sheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM images reveal additional morphological characteristics of Ni/NiFe-LDH (Figure 1d,e), indicating that the coarse Ni metal layer is homogeneously distributed across a slick NiFe-LDH sheet.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni/NiFe-LDH/IF exhibits lattice fringes of 0.23 nm (NiFe-LDH (015)) and 0.20 nm (Ni (011)); SAED shows diffraction rings for NiFe-LDH (015),(113) and Ni (011),(103).
nodes.evidence_snippet: A high-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) image of Ni/NiFe-LDH is presented in Figure 1f. It exhibits distinct lattice fringe spacings of 0.23 and 0.20 nm corresponding to the NiFe-LDH (0 1 5) and Ni (0 1 1) crystal planes...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni, Fe, O homogeneously distributed in Ni/NiFe-LDH nanoflakes; higher Ni content in shell confirmed by line scan.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) selected area mappings (Figures 1g and S7) also exhibited the same results... A compositional line profile across Ni/NiFe-LDH sheets obtained via EDS line scanning reveals that the Ni content in the shell part is significantly higher...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni/NiFe-LDH/IF shows characteristic NiFe-LDH peaks (PDF #51-0463); weak Ni (011) peak at 44.5° consistent with TEM.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni/NiFe-LDH/IF displayed the same characteristic peaks as NiFe-LDH (PDF #51-0463)... the Ni (0 1 1) peak is detected at 44.5° for the glass sample...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni/NiFe-LDH/IF Fe 2p: 713.90 eV (Fe²⁺), 711.21 eV (Fe³⁺), 705.74 eV (Fe⁰); Ni 2p: 856.60 eV (Ni³⁺), 855.18 eV (Ni²⁺), 852.78 eV (Ni⁰); O 1s: 529.6 eV (M-O), 531.1 eV (O defects), 532.2 eV (adsorbed H₂O); Fe peaks shift positively, Ni peaks shift negatively indicating electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe 2p spectrum of Ni/NiFe-LDH/IF was fitted with two spin-orbit doublets. The peak at 713.90 eV (Fe 2p₃/₂) can be ascribed to Fe²⁺, whereas 711.21 eV (Fe 2p₃/₂) can be vest in Fe³⁺. Moreover... in the Ni region (Figure 2d), the peaks at 856.60 eV (Ni³⁺), 855.18 eV (Ni²⁺) and 852.78 eV (Ni⁰) are ascribed to Ni 2p₃/₂... Shown as the peak separations in Figure 2c,d, the Fe XPS peaks of Ni/NiFe-LDH/IF exhibit positive shifts, while the Ni peaks are shifted to lower energies...

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LDH/IF Ni/Fe ratio = 0.56; Ni/NiFe-LDH/IF Ni/Fe ratio = 0.76; Ni metal loading = 2.20-2.38 mg/cm².
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the corrosion method... the Ni/Fe ratio increased from 0.56 to 0.76 (Table S1) and the Ni metal loading varied between 2.20 and 2.38 mg cm⁻² (Table S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni/NiFe-LDH/IF shows highest Cdl of 31.37 mF cm⁻² indicating largest ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Ni/NiFe-LDH/IF electrode exhibited the highest Cdl value of 31.37 mF cm⁻², suggesting that the electrode possessed the highest active surface area...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni/NiFe-LDH/IF shows Rct ≈ 0.6 Ω, lower than NiFe-LDH/IF (1.7 Ω).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the charge transfer impedance (Rct) of Ni/NiFe-LDH/IF (approximately 0.6 Ω) is significantly lower than that of NiFe-LDH/IF (1.7 Ω)...

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LDH work function = 4.74 eV; pure Ni work function = 6.26 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The work functions of NiFe-LDH (4.74 eV) and pure Ni (6.26 eV) were measured via UPS (Figure S28c).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LDH band gap = 3.21 eV from Tauc plot.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The band gap of NiFe-LDH (3.21 eV) was derived from the Tauc plot of the UV-vis spectrum (Figure S28b).
